{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement UI and client-side behavior to match the authoritative contract facts and the rollback change. Key enforced constraints and behaviors (must match server):

- Title length ceiling and validation
  - Enforce max length = 80 code points on user-entered titles. Include this exact contract marker in the prompt text: [FACT:request-title-max-length]
  - Trim leading and trailing U+0020 (space) on user input before measuring length (request.title.trim = "U+0020").
  - Count length in Unicode code points (request.title.length_unit = "unicode_code_point").
  - Enforce minimum length = 3 code points on user-entered titles (request.title.min_length = 3). The minimum and trim rules are not to be revoked.
  - If the user explicitly submits a title that violates min/max after trim, show validation errors client-side and prevent submit; if the client nevertheless sends an invalid title, handle a 422 response gracefully.
  - Ensure the UI error for invalid title uses the expected server status: 422 (request.title.invalid_status = 422).

- Read and display behavior
  - Allow reading and displaying existing titles that are longer than 80 code points without truncation. This is required by contract: [FACT:read-existing-overlength-title-allowed]
  - Do not modify or silently truncate titles when rendering. If desirable, add a visual indicator (e.g., "overlength") but do not change stored value on read.

- Update semantics (partial updates)
  - Do not revalidate the existing stored title when the user omits the title field in an update request. This behavior is required: [FACT:update-omitted_title-revalidate]
  - Concretely: when submitting a partial update (PATCH) that omits title, do not block the update client-side due to the stored title's length; send the request without title and expect the server to accept it.
  - When the user explicitly edits/supplies title in an update, apply the same trim + length validation rules as on create.

- Create vs Update
  - Create flows must require a title (create.title.required = true); validate trim, length unit, min 3 and max 80 before submission.
  - Update flows must allow omitting title (update.title.required = false); omission means "unchanged" (update.title.omission = "unchanged").

- Description
  - Keep description max length = 500 (request.description.max_length = 500); validate on client-side similarly.
  - Do not change description trimming behavior: request.description.trim = false.

- Tests to include in frontend test-suite (automated + manual QA steps)
  1) Read test: fetch an existing asset whose stored title length is 100 code points. Confirm UI displays the full title unchanged. This validates [FACT:read-existing-overlength_title_allowed].
  2) Partial update test: start with an asset that has an existing 100-code-point title, open edit form, change only the description, leave title field empty/omitted, submit PATCH. Confirm client does NOT block the submission and server accepts the update (no title sent). This confirms partial update semantics ("已有 100 字 title，更新 description").
  3) Explicit overlength submit: attempt to edit title to 90+ code points, trim spaces, see client-side validation error; if bypassed, server responds 422 and UI surfaces the server validation error.
  4) Create test: try creating with title length <3 or >80 after trim; client must block and show error.

- Error handling and UX
  - Surface server 422 errors for title validation as field-level errors and preserve input for user correction.
  - If server returns an error due to title on update, ensure you treat it as an explicit-submission validation failure (different from omission behavior).

- Deployment notes
  - Do not attempt to migrate or rewrite stored titles on the client; preserve existing overlength titles when reading/updating.
  - Coordinate with backend to ensure version bump of the asset contract/schema is applied server-side when this change is deployed (backend will handle the version increment)."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement server-side validation and behavior to match the authoritative contract facts and rollback requirement. Required explicit contract markers must be observed in this prompt: [FACT:request-title-max-length] [FACT:read-existing-overlength-title-allowed] [FACT:update-omitted_title-revalidate]

Validation rules (apply on create and on requests that explicitly include title):
- Trim rule: Trim only U+0020 (space) from both ends of request.title before validation (request.title.trim = "U+0020").
- Length unit: measure title length in Unicode code points (request.title.length_unit = "unicode_code_point").
- Minimum: require at least 3 code points (request.title.min_length = 3). This lower bound must not be revoked.
- Maximum: reject titles longer than 80 code points (request.title.max_length = 80). When a submitted title violates max (or min), return HTTP 422 with a field-level error for title. Ensure the API uses the invalid status defined (request.title.invalid_status = 422).

Read and stored-data behavior:
- Allow existing stored titles that exceed 80 code points to be read and returned by the API (read.existing_overlength_title.allowed = true). Do not reject or rewrite existing data on reads.
- Do not perform automatic trimming/truncation of stored titles in read responses beyond the trim rule applied to incoming requests; do not silently alter stored values.

Update semantics (PATCH/PUT):
- If the request omits the title field entirely, do NOT revalidate the stored title. Omission means "unchanged"; accept the update regardless of the stored title's current length or validity. This is mandated: [FACT:update-omitted_title-revalidate]
  - Concretely, for PATCH: if 'title' is absent in the JSON payload, do not run title validators; leave stored title unchanged.
- If the request includes a title field (even if equal to the existing value), apply full validation: trim U+0020, count code points, enforce min and max; on violation return 422.

Create vs Update behavior:
- Create: title is required (create.title.required = true). Validate trim, min, max on create.
- Update: title is optional (update.title.required = false); omission = unchanged (update.title.omission = "unchanged").

Description behavior:
- Continue to enforce description.max_length = 500 (request.description.max_length = 500). request.description.trim = false (do not trim description by default).

Error responses and formats:
- Use HTTP 422 for validation failures on title and description. Provide a field-level error object identifying the field, the rule failed (e.g., "min_length", "max_length") and a human message.
- Example error payload for title too long:
  { "status": 422, "errors": [{ "field": "title", "code": "max_length", "message": "title must be at most 80 Unicode code points" }] }

Data migration and versioning:
- Do NOT rewrite or delete existing overlength titles as part of this change.
- Bump the asset/contract version or schema version as part of this deployment to indicate a rollback of the max length; ensure the new deployed version number is incremented (the asset version must continue to increase after this rollback).

Tests to include in backend test-suite (automated):
1) Read test: store a title of 100 Unicode code points; GET returns full stored title. Confirms [FACT:read-existing_overlength_title_allowed].
2) Partial update test: GIVEN stored title = 100 code points, accept PATCH that omits title but changes description; stored title remains unchanged and update succeeds. Confirms [FACT:update-omitted_title_revalidate].
3) Explicit update test: when client sends title trimmed to >80 code points, respond 422 with appropriate field-level error. Confirms [FACT:request-title-max-length].
4) Create test: reject title <3 or >80 after trimming with 422.

Implementation notes:
- Ensure trimming logic uses only U+0020; do not remove other whitespace by default.
- Use a Unicode-aware code point counter (not grapheme clusters unless contract changes) to measure length.
- Maintain backward compatibility for reads: existing overlength titles remain readable and unchanged until/if a future migration is explicitly specified.

Deployment coordination:
- Communicate to frontend that omitted-title updates will not revalidate stored title, and that overlength stored titles are expected and allowed to be read.
- Increment the asset/contract version upon deploying this change so consumers can observe that the contract was updated."
  }
}
